newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds softer, await RBA rate hints.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds softer, await RBA rate hints.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed softer after the upside again proved a tough call given that the market has factored in all the positive news, including the possibility of a rate cut.
*Market now awaits RBA's Bulletin for hints on policy.

The Australian bond market and bill futures closed softer after the upside again proved a difficult task given that the market has factored in all the positive news, including the possibility of a rate cut.
The 10-year bond yield got close to testing 7.50 percent in early trading, but the absence of local data in a thin market saw some profits booked after the recent steep rally.
"Hopefully, the likelihood of a November rate cut will be much clearer after the release of the Reserve Bank's quarterly economic report on Wednesday," Nomura Research said in a report.

Economists at Nomura said the main points to look for in the report will be the RBA's outlook for business investment and its attitude towards the rate of wages growth, along with the international economic outlook.

"Any downgrading of the outlook for the international economies, especially the United States, Japan and East Asia, could suggest that another "insurance" interest rate cut is necessary," Nomura said.
The market has fully priced in a 50 basis point cut in current 7.0 percent official interest rates, which is seen mostly likely to occur after the RBA board meets in November.
Dresdner Bank also considers that the odds of another rate cut have narrowed sufficiently to change its view on interest rates, provided the data over the few weeks behave as expected.
This includes next week's quarterly inflation and wages.

"The reasons for our revisions are: the unemployment rate is now trending up; business sentiment remains weak; leading indicators, eg housing, are soft; inflation is set to come back to 2-3 percent; and the wages outlook is benign," the bank said.
The New South Wales state government joined the calls, saying a rate cut was needed stimulate a flat labour market and head off the effects of the Federal government's spending cuts.

Local bonds underperformed other dollar bloc markets in fairly thin trade as they also awaited for the U.S. bond market to get back into full swing after Monday's holiday. This was most notable against NZ which built on Monday's post-election rally after a modest rise in its quarterly inflation report.

The 10-year bond contract scored a new dayside high of 92.495 just after opening where the market found stiff resistance and later slithered back through support at 92.440, although further falls are seen limited, traders added.
